claim.quote: We report the four most significant SPT detections of SZ clusters in this field, three of which were previously unknown and, therefore, represent the first galaxy clusters discovered with an SZ survey.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal publication date was not read from a fetched source.

name: Galaxy clusters discovered with a Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect survey

official_url.quote: Galaxy clusters discovered with a Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect survey

significance.quote: The SZ clusters are detected as decrements with greater than 5-sigma significance in the high-sensitivity 150 GHz SPT map.
significance.value: Clusters detected as decrements with greater than 5-sigma significance in the 150 GHz SPT map

summary.plain: The South Pole Telescope found the first galaxy clusters ever discovered by their imprint on the Big Bang afterglow (the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect), three of which were previously unknown.
summary.technical: SPT 40 deg^2 BCS field, two seasons at 95/150/225 GHz: four clusters detected at >5 sigma in the 150 GHz map, three new, with SZ spectrum confirmed in the 95 and 225 GHz maps and optical confirmation (z ~ 0.4 and z > ~ 0.8).

title: Galaxy clusters discovered with a Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect survey
why_it_matters: The abstract says these first four clusters demonstrate "that SZ surveys, and the SPT in particular, can be an effective means for finding galaxy clusters".
